<reason>A made the stronger comparison between compulsory recovery attempts and incentives rewarding actual waste reduction. B plausibly argued that large stores already possess clearance tools, but did not adequately weigh additional recovery against labor and timing costs. Its pressure answer rejected last-minute theater without resolving when a meaningful selling window must begin. A answered its own pressure questions directly and conceded that some compulsory discounts would help. B increasingly defended the sequence itself rather than explaining why its benefits justified the requirement.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A exposed the asymmetry in B’s objection that disposal fees let stores “pay and keep wasting”: the mandate also permits disposal after expenditure on an unsuccessful markdown. A then explained that fees can induce recovery and better ordering, leaving B’s distinction between “Plan A” and “residual” disposal insufficient to establish superior outcomes.</best_rebuttal>
